newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigerian share index at record high in heavy trade.
newsitem.headline: Nigerian share index at record high in heavy trade.

text.p: The Nigerian stock exchange all-share index recorded its biggest rise of the week on Friday, closing at a record high, traders said.
It shot up by 22.05 points to 6698.79 from 6676.74 on Thursday, buoyed by big jumps in oil and food shares.
Traders said the rise was encouraging considering current bear sentiments depressing blue chip stocks. "Some favourable trading results also helped during the week," one trader said.
The oil marketing companies, whose shares are the toast of the market, rose as investors showed healthy appetite for them.

National Oil, whose mid-year result is still being expected, jumped 60 kobo up to 40.60 naira. Unipetrol was 49.00 naira, up 40 kobo, while African Petroleum at 37.80 naira, Agip at 17.00 naira and Mobil at 43.80 naira notched 30 kobo apiece.
Total closed 25 kobo up at 52.00 naira, still the dearest stock in the market.
Nestle led food shares with a one naira rise to 42.00 naira while Nigerian Tobacco Company's good run persisted with a 15 kobo jump to 3.41 naira.

Cadbury, sliding recently, was steady on Friday after announcing an increase in third-quarter profits. After-tax profit rose to 313 million naira in the period to end-September from 233.8 million naira in the same period last year.
Conglomerates were down again, with Lever Brothers closing 10 kobo lower at 24.85 naira. UAC lost 20 kobo at 9.00 naira and SCOA fell by two kobo to 2.33 naira.
Guinness shed 30 kobo to 6.25 naira while the sector's giant Nigerian Breweries added 20 kobo to 12.60 naira.

Banks were also under pressure. Afribank and Guaranty Trust Bank lost 10 kobo at 4.90 naira and 13.50 naira, respectively while FSB International Bank notched 10 kobo to 5.20 naira. Union Bank slid by five to 6.60 naira.
Traders said besides oil shares, low priced insurance stocks and Benue Cement would continue to do well in the weeks ahead.
"Benue Cement is rising on its good third-quarter showing and because it is selling below the market leaders," one said.
On Friday, it gained five kobo to 7.85 naira.
AIICO Insurance, top of the class in that sector, finished 10 kobo up at 8.40 naira. Guinea Insurance was two up at 75 kobo.
